newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foodland sees higher Progressive profit.
newsitem.headline: Foodland sees higher Progressive profit.

text.p: Food retailer and wholesaler Foodland Associated Ltd said on Thursday it expected a higher second half contribution from its 58 percent owned New Zealand based supermarket Progressive Enterprises Ltd.

"We expect an improved contribution from Progressives in the second half as maangement further strengthens operating and finacial controls, improves margins and further reduces debt through the sale of non-core assets," Foodland managing director Barry Alty said in a statement.
Foodland earlier reported a 34.7 percent lift in net profit to A$28.7 million for the six months ended January 31, 1997.

"The results we are announcing today reflect improved profitability from the sales growth of Action in Western Australia, improved trading margins and operating efficiencies at Farmers Deka and the correction of many poor operating practices which produced an entirely unsatisfactory Progressive result during the previous corresponding half," Alty said.
Last week, Progressive reported a half year net profit of NZ$8.02 million up from NZ$2.2 million a year earlier.
At 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT), Foodland shares were 22 cents or 3.28 percent up at A$6.92.
